package.name: bonbon_distributed_network_monitor
package.description:
Chrony clock-offset monitoring for the three-Pi deployment -- the package config/distributed/robot_network.yaml's own header and docs/INTER_PI_COMMUNICATION_POLICY.md's Rule 9 have named since the three-Pi architecture was designed, but that was never actually built until now.
Distinct from bonbon_distributed_safety (which already does real, tested peer-Pi liveness detection via heartbeat staleness) -- this package answers a different question: "are the three Pis' clocks still within config/distributed/robot_network.yaml's time_sync .alert_offset_ms of each other," which heartbeat staleness alone cannot detect (a Pi can be heartbeating on time while its clock has drifted, which silently corrupts cross-Pi event ordering and heartbeat-staleness math itself -- see Rule 9's own rationale).
Runs on every Pi (chrony's own offset applies locally to whichever Pi it's sampled on, not just Pi-3 the NTP server) via `chronyc tracking`, parsed by core/chrony_offset.py (pure Python, no subprocess dependency at parse time so it's fully unit-testable), and forwards a real bonbon_msgs/HalFault into the ALREADY-EXISTING /bonbon/hal/fault ingestion topic bonbon_fault_manager consumes -- no second alerting mechanism is built here.
